from manim import *
import numpy as np

SILVER = "#C0C0C0"

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with title and lecture lines
        lecture_lines = [
            'Classical objects exist in one definite state at once.',
            'A coin is either heads or tails, never both.',
            'Quantum objects can exist in many states simultaneously.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Classical vs. Quantum Worldview", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight lecture line 1
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Classical Side: Heads and Tails side-by-side
        heads_circle = Circle(radius=0.4, color="#FFD700", fill_opacity=0.3)
        heads_label = Text("Heads", font_size=16, color="#FFD700")
        heads_group = VGroup(heads_circle, heads_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(heads_group, "C2")

        tails_circle = Circle(radius=0.4, color="#C0C0C0", fill_opacity=0.3)
        tails_label = Text("Tails", font_size=16, color="#C0C0C0")
        tails_group = VGroup(tails_circle, tails_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(tails_group, "E2")

        self.play(FadeIn(heads_group), FadeIn(tails_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight lecture line 2
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(SILVER)
        )

        # Merge and spin into a grey blur
        # Create a blur object at the Quantum side's future position
        blur_circle = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#888888", fill_opacity=0.6)
        # Add internal lines to simulate rotation/spin
        spin_lines = VGroup(*[
            Line(blur_circle.get_center(), blur_circle.get_top(), stroke_width=2, color="#888888")
            .rotate(angle, about_point=blur_circle.get_center())
            for angle in np.linspace(0, 2*PI, 8, endpoint=False)
        ])
        blur_group = VGroup(blur_circle, spin_lines)
        self.place_at_grid(blur_group, "D5")

        # Animation of merging
        self.play(
            heads_group.animate.move_to(self.grid["D5"]).set_opacity(0),
            tails_group.animate.move_to(self.grid["D5"]).set_opacity(0),
            FadeIn(blur_group),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        # Rotation logic for blur
        rotation_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        spin_lines.add_updater(lambda m: m.rotate(0.2))
        self.add(spin_lines)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight lecture line 3
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )

        # Label 'Superposition' appears above the spinning blur
        superposition_label = Text("Superposition", font_size=20, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(superposition_label, "B5")

        # Vertical divider separates Classical from Quantum
        # Grid col 3 ends at x=2.5, col 4 starts at x=3.5. Midpoint is 3.0.
        divider_line = Line(
            start=[3.0, 3.0, 0],
            end=[3.0, -3.0, 0],
            color="#555555",
            stroke_width=2
        )
        
        classical_header = Text("Classical", font_size=18, color="#555555")
        quantum_header = Text("Quantum", font_size=18, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(classical_header, "A2")
        self.place_at_grid(quantum_header, "A5")

        # Pulse glow for the Quantum side
        quantum_glow = Circle(radius=0.8, color="#FFFFFF", stroke_width=0, fill_opacity=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(quantum_glow, "D5")
        
        self.play(
            Create(divider_line),
            Write(superposition_label),
            FadeIn(classical_header),
            FadeIn(quantum_header),
            FadeIn(quantum_glow)
        )

        # Pulse animation
        glow_tracker = ValueTracker(0.1)
        quantum_glow.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_fill(opacity=glow_tracker.get_value()))
        
        self.play(
            glow_tracker.animate.set_value(0.4),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=2
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

        # Cleanup updaters
        spin_lines.remove_updater(spin_lines.updaters[0])
        quantum_glow.remove_updater(quantum_glow.updaters[0])

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Prerequisite: The Vector State Representation", 
            [
                "We represent quantum states as arrows called vectors.", 
                "The ket symbol denotes a specific quantum state.", 
                "Think of it as a compass pointing between states."
            ]
        )

        # Colors
        COLOR_0 = "#00FF00" # Green
        COLOR_1 = "#0000FF" # Blue
        COLOR_PSI = "#FFFF00" # Yellow
        COLOR_PROJ = "#888888" # Gray

        # Origin point for our coordinate system
        origin = self.grid["E2"]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_0))

        # Vertical green arrow for |0> (Y-axis)
        arrow_0 = Arrow(start=origin, end=self.grid["B2"], color=COLOR_0, buff=0)
        # Use Text instead of MathTex to avoid 'latex' FileNotFoundError
        label_0 = Text("|0⟩", color=COLOR_0, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(label_0, "B2")
        label_0.shift(UP * 0.3)

        # Horizontal blue arrow for |1> (X-axis)
        arrow_1 = Arrow(start=origin, end=self.grid["E5"], color=COLOR_1, buff=0)
        label_1 = Text("|1⟩", color=COLOR_1, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(label_1, "E5")
        label_1.shift(RIGHT * 0.4)

        self.play(
            GrowArrow(arrow_0),
            Write(label_0),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(arrow_1),
            Write(label_1),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_1))

        # Yellow vector |psi> at 45 degrees
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(45 * DEGREES)
        psi_len = 2.5
        
        psi_arrow = Arrow(
            start=origin, 
            end=origin + np.array([np.cos(angle_tracker.get_value()), np.sin(angle_tracker.get_value()), 0]) * psi_len,
            color=COLOR_PSI,
            buff=0
        )
        
        label_psi = Text("|ψ⟩", color=COLOR_PSI, font_size=32)
        # Position label_psi at the tip of the arrow
        label_psi.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(
            psi_arrow.get_end() + 0.4 * (psi_arrow.get_end() - origin) / np.linalg.norm(psi_arrow.get_end() - origin)
        ))

        # Projection lines
        def get_proj_x():
            tip = psi_arrow.get_end()
            return DashedLine(
                start=tip,
                end=np.array([tip[0], origin[1], 0]),
                color=COLOR_PROJ,
                stroke_width=2
            )

        def get_proj_y():
            tip = psi_arrow.get_end()
            return DashedLine(
                start=tip,
                end=np.array([origin[0], tip[1], 0]),
                color=COLOR_PROJ,
                stroke_width=2
            )

        proj_x = always_redraw(get_proj_x)
        proj_y = always_redraw(get_proj_y)

        # Growth animation for |psi>
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(psi_arrow),
            Write(label_psi),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(
            Create(proj_x),
            Create(proj_y),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_PSI))

        # Update psi_arrow tip based on tracker
        psi_arrow.add_updater(lambda a: a.become(
            Arrow(
                start=origin, 
                end=origin + np.array([np.cos(angle_tracker.get_value()), np.sin(angle_tracker.get_value()), 0]) * psi_len,
                color=COLOR_PSI,
                buff=0
            )
        ))

        # Rotate |psi> towards |0> (90 degrees / PI/2)
        self.play(
            angle_tracker.animate.set_value(90 * DEGREES),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=slow_into
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the scene
        lecture_lines = [
            'The state Psi combines basis states zero and one.',
            'Alpha and Beta represent probability amplitudes of each.',
            'These amplitudes are complex numbers describing the system.',
            'Squaring these numbers gives the probability of each outcome.',
            'Quark the Cat exists as a combination of paths.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Quantum State (Psi)", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Equation |ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩ fades in center screen
        main_eq = VGroup(
            Text("|ψ⟩", font_size=32), 
            Text("=", font_size=32), 
            Text("α", font_size=32), 
            Text("|0⟩", font_size=32), 
            Text("+", font_size=32), 
            Text("β", font_size=32), 
            Text("|1⟩", font_size=32)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.15).set_color(WHITE)
        
        self.place_in_area(main_eq, "B2", "C5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            Write(main_eq)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Alpha (#FF00FF) and Beta (#00FFFF) variables glow and enlarge.
        alpha_part = main_eq[2]
        beta_part = main_eq[5]
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        self.play(
            alpha_part.animate.scale(1.3).set_color("#FF00FF"),
            beta_part.animate.scale(1.3).set_color("#00FFFF"),
            Flash(alpha_part, color="#FF00FF"),
            Flash(beta_part, color="#00FFFF")
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        complex_label = Text("α, β ∈ ℂ", font_size=28, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(complex_label, "D1", "D2", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(complex_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        prob_eq = Text("|α|² + |β|² = 1", font_size=28, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_in_area(prob_eq, "E2", "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(prob_eq))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        cat_eq = Text(
            "|Quark⟩ ≈ 0.7|Left⟩ + 0.7|Right⟩",
            font_size=24,
            color=WHITE
        )
        self.place_in_area(cat_eq, "F1", "F6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(cat_eq))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Reset colors and finish
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with specific teaching content
        lecture_lines = [
            'If two states exist, their combination is also possible.',
            'This linear combination creates a new, valid quantum state.',
            'Like musical notes forming a chord, states blend together.',
            'Wave interference shows how these states interact and add.',
            'Superposition allows for complex harmonies in quantum systems.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Principle of Superposition", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_CYAN = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_ORANGE = "#FF8C00"
        COLOR_WHITE = "#FFFFFF"
        
        # ValueTrackers for dynamic animation
        phase_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Description: Cyan sine wave enters
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_CYAN)
        wave_cyan = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: 0.7 * np.sin(2.5 * x), 
            x_range=[-1.5, 1.5], 
            color=COLOR_CYAN
        )
        self.place_in_area(wave_cyan, "A1", "B6")
        self.play(FadeIn(wave_cyan, shift=RIGHT))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Description: Orange sine wave enters
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_ORANGE)
        wave_orange = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: 0.7 * np.sin(2.5 * x), 
            x_range=[-1.5, 1.5], 
            color=COLOR_ORANGE
        )
        self.place_in_area(wave_orange, "E1", "F6")
        self.play(FadeIn(wave_orange, shift=LEFT))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Description: Waves overlap to create white constructive interference chord
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_WHITE)
        
        # Calculate target center for the combined visualization (C1-D6 area)
        mid_tl = self.grid["C1"]
        mid_br = self.grid["D6"]
        mid_center = (mid_tl + mid_br) / 2

        # Create the sum wave (initially constructive since phase is 0)
        sum_wave = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: 0.7 * (np.sin(2.5 * x) + np.sin(2.5 * x)),
            x_range=[-1.5, 1.5],
            color=COLOR_WHITE,
            stroke_width=5
        ).move_to(mid_center)

        self.play(
            wave_cyan.animate.move_to(mid_center).set_stroke(opacity=0.3),
            wave_orange.animate.move_to(mid_center).set_stroke(opacity=0.3),
            Create(sum_wave),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Description: Interaction label and constructive peak focus
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_WHITE)
        
        label_c = Text("Constructive Peak", font_size=18, color=COLOR_WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label_c, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(label_c))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Description: Phase shift to show destructive interference (flat line)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_WHITE)
        
        # Update the sum wave based on phase tracker value
        sum_wave.add_updater(lambda m: m.become(
            FunctionGraph(
                lambda x: 0.7 * (np.sin(2.5 * x) + np.sin(2.5 * x + phase_tracker.get_value())),
                x_range=[-1.5, 1.5],
                color=COLOR_WHITE,
                stroke_width=5
            ).move_to(mid_center)
        ))
        
        label_d = Text("Destructive Cancellation", font_size=18, color=COLOR_WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label_d, "E3", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Animate the transition to destructive interference
        self.play(
            phase_tracker.animate.set_value(PI),
            ReplacementTransform(label_c, label_d),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            'Classical bits are either zero or one, like switches.',
            'Qubits use superposition to be both states at once.',
            'Quantum computers solve complex problems exponentially faster.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Application: Quantum Computing Power", lecture_lines)
        
        # Initialize lecture colors (all gray first, then highlight)
        for line in self.lecture:
            line.set_color(GRAY)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Description: A classical switch flips between 0 and 1 (#FFFFFF).
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        switch_frame = Rectangle(height=1.2, width=2.4, color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
        switch_knob = Square(side_length=1.0, fill_opacity=1, color=WHITE)
        # Position knob at '0' position (left)
        switch_knob.move_to(switch_frame.get_left() + RIGHT * 0.6)
        
        label_0 = Text("0", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        label_1 = Text("1", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        
        switch_container = VGroup(switch_frame, switch_knob)
        self.place_in_area(switch_container, "B2", "D5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        label_0.next_to(switch_frame, LEFT, buff=0.3)
        label_1.next_to(switch_frame, RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        
        line1_group = VGroup(switch_container, label_0, label_1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(line1_group))
        self.wait(0.5)
        # Flip to 1
        self.play(switch_knob.animate.move_to(switch_frame.get_right() - RIGHT * 0.6), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(0.5)
        # Flip back to 0
        self.play(switch_knob.animate.move_to(switch_frame.get_left() + RIGHT * 0.6), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Description: A green glowing Qubit (#00FF00) displays 0 and 1 overlapping.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"),
            FadeOut(line1_group)
        )
        
        qubit_circle = Circle(radius=1.2, color="#00FF00", stroke_width=6)
        # Semi-transparent fill for glow
        qubit_glow = Circle(radius=1.4, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.2, stroke_width=0)
        
        # Superposition labels
        label_sup_0 = Text("0", font_size=48, color="#00FF00").shift(LEFT * 0.2)
        label_sup_1 = Text("1", font_size=48, color="#00FF00").shift(RIGHT * 0.2)
        
        qubit_group = VGroup(qubit_circle, qubit_glow, label_sup_0, label_sup_1)
        self.place_in_area(qubit_group, "B2", "D5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(qubit_group))
        
        # Animated pulsing for superposition
        for _ in range(2):
            self.play(
                qubit_glow.animate.scale(1.2).set_opacity(0.4),
                label_sup_0.animate.set_opacity(0.5),
                label_sup_1.animate.set_opacity(1.0),
                run_time=0.8,
                rate_func=there_and_back
            )
            self.play(
                qubit_glow.animate.scale(1.2).set_opacity(0.4),
                label_sup_0.animate.set_opacity(1.0),
                label_sup_1.animate.set_opacity(0.5),
                run_time=0.8,
                rate_func=there_and_back
            )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Description: Maze paths highlight simultaneously in glowing yellow (#FFFF00).
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GRAY),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            FadeOut(qubit_group)
        )
        
        # Maze structure using grid points
        start_node = Dot(self.grid["D1"], color=WHITE, radius=0.15)
        end_node = Dot(self.grid["D6"], color=WHITE, radius=0.15)
        
        # Define 3 distinct paths
        p1 = VMobject().set_points_as_corners([self.grid["D1"], self.grid["B2"], self.grid["B5"], self.grid["D6"]])
        p2 = VMobject().set_points_as_corners([self.grid["D1"], self.grid["D3"], self.grid["D6"]])
        p3 = VMobject().set_points_as_corners([self.grid["D1"], self.grid["F2"], self.grid["F5"], self.grid["D6"]])
        
        paths = VGroup(p1, p2, p3).set_color(GRAY_E).set_stroke(width=3)
        
        self.play(Create(paths), FadeIn(start_node), FadeIn(end_node))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Quantum exploration: highlight all paths simultaneously in yellow
        quantum_paths = paths.copy().set_color("#FFFF00").set_stroke(width=6)
        
        self.play(Create(quantum_paths), run_time=2)
        
        # Exit indicator
        exit_glow = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=0.5, stroke_width=0).move_to(self.grid["D6"])
        self.play(FadeIn(exit_glow, scale=0.1))
        self.play(exit_glow.animate.scale(2).set_opacity(0), run_time=1)

        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: The Mystery of 'Both': Understanding Superposition and Quantum States
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate science students or advanced high school students

sections.title: The Classical vs. Quantum Worldview
sections.content: Introduce the fundamental difference between classical certainty and quantum probability. In the classical world, an object is in one state (on/off, up/down). In the quantum world, objects can exist in multiple states simultaneously.
sections.example: A spinning coin on a table: While spinning, it isn't 'Heads' or 'Tails' yet, but a blur of both. In the quantum world, the coin remains in this 'blur' until we stop it.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Vector State Representation
sections.content: Introduce the Dirac notation (Bra-Ket) and the idea of a state as a vector. Use a 2D coordinate system where the X-axis represents state |0> and the Y-axis represents state |1>. Explain that any arrow (vector) drawn between them is a valid state.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'State Compass': If North is |0> (Off) and East is |1> (On), a quantum state can point North-East, representing a mix of both directions.

sections.title: Defining the Quantum State (Psi)
sections.content: Present the mathematical formula |ψ> = α|0> + β|1>. Define α (alpha) and β (beta) as 'probability amplitudes.' Emphasize that these are complex numbers whose squares ( |α|² and |β|² ) determine the probability of finding the system in that state.
sections.example: A character named 'Quark the Cat' standing at a fork in the road. In quantum mechanics, Quark doesn't choose left or right; he exists as a mathematical combination of both paths: |Quark> = 0.7|Left> + 0.7|Right>.

sections.title: The Principle of Superposition
sections.content: Explain that if a quantum system can be in state A or state B, it can also be in a linear combination of both. Use wave interference graphics to show how states can add together constructively or destructively.
sections.example: Musical Harmony: Just as a single chord is a superposition of several distinct notes played at once, a quantum state is a 'harmony' of all possible physical configurations.

sections.title: Measurement and State Collapse
sections.content: Explain the 'Measurement Problem.' When an observer measures the system, the superposition 'collapses' into one of the basis states (|0> or |1>). This is a non-reversible transition from probability to certainty.
sections.example: The 'Mystery Box' animation: A particle is bouncing everywhere inside a box (superposition). The moment a camera looks inside, the particle 'snaps' to one specific corner instantly.

sections.title: Application: Quantum Computing Power
sections.content: Conclude by explaining why this matters. A classical bit is a switch (0 or 1), but a Qubit (Quantum Bit) uses superposition to perform multiple calculations at once, leading to exponential processing power.
sections.example: A maze-solving robot: A classical robot tries every path one by one. A quantum robot in superposition enters every path simultaneously, finding the exit in a single 'step'.

lecture_lines: Classical objects exist in one definite state at once.
But quantum states can merge into a single blur.
This combined state is known as quantum superposition.
A clear boundary separates the classical and quantum worlds.
The quantum side pulses with all possible outcomes.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Vector State Representation

storyboard.title: The Principle of Superposition
lecture_lines: Adding two valid quantum states creates another valid state.

The original quantum blur is lost upon measurement.
